prompt.body: 90s hard rock at 140 BPM in A major. The album closer. Slash's Les Paul, palm-muted chug, but the song opens with a single clean electric guitar note that builds — the only quiet moment on the album. The vocalist is Axl Rose circa Use Your Illusion II — restrained in the opening verse, wailing on the held notes, screaming on the chorus. The drummer is half-time backbeat on the verse and opens up to a full double-kick backbeat on the chorus. The bass is thick, palm-muted, root notes. The chorus is a gang shout with three-part vocal harmony. Slash-style solo with screaming bends, slow bends, a sustained high note at the end — the last solo on the album. No piano, no synth, no ballad-section piano. The lyrics are a defiant closing statement — 'They said I'd never make it, said I'd burn out by twenty-five, they said the band would break, the van would die, the songs wouldn't survive.' The chorus is the answer: 'Standing still, every scar a flag I fly.' Think GnR 'Civil War' or Skid Row 'Youth Gone Wild' (the slow version) — long-form 90s hard rock anthem, the album closer, the song that says we made it. Production: 1991, the Les Paul is the lead voice, the drums are huge, the crowd noise at the end is the audience singing along. FIRE.
